εἶπε, Βλασφήμησον. Οἱ γὰρ πονηρὰ συμ βουλεύοντες οὐ τολμῶσιν
ἀνακεκαλυμμένην εἰσά γειν τὴν συμβουλήν. Τί λέγεις, ὦ γύναι; ∆έον ἐξι λεώσασθαι,
δέον καταλλάξαι, παροξῦναι μᾶλλον παρ αινεῖς; Εἰ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ταῦτα ἐποίησε,
παρακαλέσαι αὐτὸν, οὐ βλασφημῆσαι δεῖ. Πόθεν δὲ δῆλον, ὅτι καὶ ἐρώμενον
τελευτήσω; Πλὴν ὅρα ὅπως εἶχε περὶ τῆς βλασφημίας ἡ γυνή. Ὥσπερ παραχρῆμα
αὐτὴν θάνατον ἐπάγειν ἱκανὴν ἡγεῖτο. Στ. ιʹ. Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυ
ρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν; Ὁ γὰρ μακάριος οὗτος, πανταχόθεν βαλλόμενος,
ἀσφαλέστερον ἵστατο, καὶ μυρία βέλη δεχόμενος, οὐκ ἐνεδίδου. Ἀλλ' ἐκένωσε μὲν
τοῦ διαβόλου τὴν βελοθή κην, αὐτὸς δὲ οὐ κατέπεσεν, οὐδὲ ὑπεσκελίσθη. Ἀλλ'
ὥσπερ ἄριστος κυβερνήτης, οὔτε μαινομένης τῆς θα λάσσης, καὶ τῶν κυμάτων
διεγειρομένων κατεποντί ζετο, οὔτε γαλήνης οὔσης ῥᾳθυμότερος ἐγίνετο. Ἀλλ' ἐν
ἑκατέρᾳ τῇ τῶν καιρῶν διαφορᾷ ἴσην τὴν ἑαυτοῦ τέχνην διετήρησε. Καὶ οὔτε
πλοῦτος ἑαυτὸν ἐφύ σησεν, οὔτε πενία ἐταπείνωσεν, οὔτε, κατὰ ῥοῦν τῶν
πραγμάτων φερομένων, ὕπτιος ἦν καὶ ἀναπεπτωκὼς, οὔτε, ὅλης σχεδὸν τῆς οἰκείας
ἀνατραπείσης, καὶ πανολεθρίας γενομένης, διεταράχθη, καὶ τὴν ἀνδρίαν ἤλεγξε τὴν
ἑαυτοῦ. Ἀκουέτωσαν πλούσιοι, ἀκουέτω σαν πένητες· ἑκατέροις γὰρ τὸ διήγημα
χρήσιμον, καὶ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ἡ ἱστορία λυσιτελής· καὶ τοῖς ἐν εὐημερίᾳ, καὶ τοῖς
ἐν συμφοραῖς. Ἑκάτερα γὰρ τὰ ὅπλα μεταχειρίσας ὁ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἀγωνιστὴς, ὁ τῆς
οἰκουμένης στεφανίτης, ἐν ἑκατέροις τὸ τρόπαιον ἔστησε· καὶ πρὸς πᾶν εἶδος
πολέμου τοῦ δαίμονος 17.64 ἐπελθόντος ἐκείνου, πρὸς ἅπαντα παρετάξατο, καὶ ἐν
πᾶσιν ἀνεκηρύττετο. Καὶ καθάπερ στρατιώτης γεν ναῖος, καὶ εἰδὼς νυκτομαχεῖν,
τειχομαχεῖν, πεζομα χεῖν, ναυμαχεῖν, καὶ τοξεύειν, καὶ δόρυ σείειν, καὶ σφενδόναις
καὶ ἀκοντίοις, καὶ παντὶ τρόπῳ μάχης περιγίνεσθαι τῆς ἐναντίων καὶ πανταχοῦ κρα
τεῖν· οὕτω δὴ καὶ ὁ γενναῖος ἐκεῖνος ἅπαντα πειρα σμὸν μετὰ πολλῆς ἤνεγκε τῆς
ἀνδρίας, τὸν ἀπὸ πε νίας, τὸν ἀπὸ λιμοῦ, τὸν ἀπὸ νόσου, τὸν ἐξ ὀδύνης, τὸν ἀπὸ
παίδων ἀπωλείας, τὸν ἀπὸ τῶν φίλων, τὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ἐχθρῶν, τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γυναικὸς,
τὸν ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκετῶν. Οὐ γὰρ ἦν ἀνθρωπίνη συμφορὰ, ἣ μὴ εἰς τὸ σῶμα ἐξεκενώθη
ἐκείνου. Ἀλλ' ὅμως ἁπάντων ὑπερηνέχθη τῶν δικτύων, καὶ ὑψηλότερος γέγονε τῶν
τοῦ διαβόλου καλάμων. Καὶ τὸ δὴ θαυμαστότερον, ὅτι καὶ πάντα αὐτῷ, καὶ πάντα
μεθ' ὑπερβολῆς, καὶ πάντα ὑφ' ἕν. Μὴ γὰρ τοῦτο ἴδῃς, ὅτι τοσαῦτα ἔπα θεν· ἀλλὰ
πρόσθες, ὅτι οὐδὲ κατὰ μικρὸν, οὐδὲ ἐκ διαστήματος, ἀλλ' ὑφὲν καὶ ὁμοῦ. Οὐ μικρὰ
δὲ αὕτη πειρασμῶν προσθήκη. Τῶν μὲν γὰρ ἄλλων ἕκαστος ἀνθρώπων πρῶτον μὲν
οὐδεὶς ἂν εὑρεθείη πάντα ὑπο μείνας ὁμοῦ, ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ πενίᾳ παλαίει, ὅμως ὑγείας
ἀπολαύει· εἰ δὲ καὶ πενίᾳ καὶ νόσῳ περιεπάρη, ἀλλὰ γυναικὸς πολλάκις ἀπήλαυσε
παραμυθουμένης τὰ δει νὰ, καὶ ἀντὶ λιμένος αὐτῷ γινομένης. Εἰ δὲ μὴ γυναι κὸς
ἀπήλαυσε τοιαύτης, ἀλλ' οὐχ οὕτω συμβουλευ θείσης ὀλέθρια, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ καὶ τοὺς
παῖδας ἀθρόον ἀπώλεσεν ἅπαντας· εἰ δὲ καὶ ἀθρόον, ἀλλ' οὐ τοιούτῳ τρόπῳ
τελευτῆς· εἰ δὲ καὶ τοιούτῳ [τρόπῳ] τελευτῆς, ἀλλὰ φίλους ἔσχε παρακαλοῦντας· εἰ
δὲ οὐκ ἔσχε πα ρακαλοῦντας, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ καὶ οὕτως ἐπεμβαίνοντας· εἰ δὲ καὶ
ἐπεμβαίνοντας, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ καὶ οἰκέτας ὀνειδί ζοντας· εἰ δὲ καὶ ὀνειδίζοντας, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ
καὶ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἐμπτύοντας· εἰ δὲ καὶ εἰς τὸ πρόσ ωπον ἐμπτύοντας, ἀλλ'
οὐχὶ καὶ νόσῳ τοιαύτῃ περιε πάρει, ἀλλὰ δωματίου καὶ σκέπης ἀπήλαυσε, καὶ οὐκ
ἐπὶ τῆς κοπρίας ἐκάθητο· εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κοπρίας ἐκάθητο, ἀλλ' ἔσχε τοὺς χεῖρα
ὀρέγοντας· εἰ δὲ μὴ ἔσχε τοὺς χεῖρα ὀρέγοντας, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ καὶ ἐπεμβαίνοντας. Οὗτος
δ' ἅπαντα ταῦτα ὑπήνεγκεν. Στίχ. ιαʹ. Παρεγένοντο ἕκαστος ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας χώ ρας πρὸς
αὐτὸν, Ἐλιφὰζ ὁ Θαιμανῶν βασι λεὺς, Βαλδὰδ ὁ Σαυχέων τύραννος, Σωφὰρ
Μιναίων βασιλεύς. Φιλικὴ μὲν ἡ παρουσία σου, φιλικὴ δὲ ἡ παρ αίνεσις. Ἐλιφάζ·
Θεός με διέσπειρεν, ἢ, Θεοῦ μου φαυλισμός. Θαιμὰν, ἔκλειψις αὐτῶν. Σωφὰρ,
σκοπὸς, ἢ φαυλισμός. Βαλδὰδ, παλαίωσις, καὶ ἐπίδοξος. Σαυχαίων, ἀδολεσχία
αὐτῶν. Στίχ. ιαʹ. Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ τρεῖς φίλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ κακὰ πάντα, τὰ ἐπελθόντα
αὐτῷ, παρε γένοντο ἕκαστος ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας χώρας πρὸς αὐτόν. Ἐάν τις ζητῇ, διὰ τί

pass_a_gloss: to recount, then she brings on the shameless counsel. And she did not even say openly to him, Blaspheme. For those who advise evil things do not dare to introduce the counsel uncovered. What are you saying, O woman? One ought to propitiate, one ought to reconcile — do you rather advise to provoke? For if God did these things, one must entreat him, not blaspheme. And from where is it clear that I will also die as a beloved one? But see how the wife held about blasphemy. As if she thought it able to bring death upon her at once. Verse 10: If we received the good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not bear the bad? For this blessed man, struck from every side, stood more securely, and receiving countless arrows, did not yield. But he emptied the devil’s quiver, and he himself did not fall, nor was he tripped. But like an excellent pilot, neither when the sea was raging and the waves were rising was he sunk, nor when there was calm did he become more careless. But in each difference of the times he kept his own skill equal. And neither did wealth puff him up, nor did poverty humble him, nor, when affairs were carried with the current, was he supine and relaxed, nor, when nearly the whole household was overturned and total destruction happened, was he disturbed and did he convict his own manliness. Let the rich hear; let the poor hear; for the narrative is useful to both, and the history beneficial to all humans — both those in prosperity and those in calamities. For having handled both weapons, the contestant of piety, the crown-bearer of the inhabited world, set up the trophy in both; and toward every kind of war of that demon who came on, he arrayed himself toward all, and in all he was proclaimed. And just as a noble soldier, knowing how to fight by night, fight walls, fight on foot, fight at sea, and shoot, and shake a spear, and with slings and javelins, and by every manner of battle to prevail over the opponents and conquer everywhere — so also that noble one bore every trial with much manliness: from poverty, from hunger, from disease, from pain, from loss of children, from friends, from enemies, from the wife, from the household servants. For there was no human calamity that was not emptied into that body. But nevertheless he was carried above all the nets, and became higher than the devil’s reeds. And the more marvelous thing: that all things came to him, and all with excess, and all under one blow. For do not look at this, that he suffered so many things; but add that not little by little, nor from an interval, but under one and together. And this is no small addition of trials. For of other humans each — first none would be found who endured all things together, but if he also wrestles with poverty, still he enjoys health; and if he was entangled in both poverty and disease, yet often he enjoyed a wife consoling the terrors and becoming a harbor for him. And if he did not enjoy such a wife, yet not one advising destructive things thus; and not also having lost all the children at once; and if at once, yet not by such a manner of death; and if by such a manner of death, yet he had friends comforting; and if he did not have comforters, yet not also insulting thus; and if insulting, yet not also household servants reproaching; and if reproaching, yet not also spitting into his face; and if spitting into his face, yet not also entangled in such a disease, but enjoyed a room and shelter, and did not sit on the dunghill; and if he sat on the dunghill, yet he had those stretching out a hand; and if he did not have those stretching out a hand, yet not also those insulting. But this one endured all these things. Verse 11: There came each from his own country to him, Eliphaz the king of the Temanites, Baldad the tyrant of the Saucheans, Sophar king of the Minaeans. Friendly is your presence; friendly also the exhortation. Eliphaz: God scattered me, or, Contempt of my God. Teman, their eclipse. Sophar, watcher, or contempt. Baldad, aging, and glorious. Of the Saucheans, their idle talk. Verse 11: And the three friends of his, having heard all the evils that had come upon him, came each from his own country to him. If someone seeks why after so much time the friends have come, let him think first that they dwelt in different countries, and after a very long time many perhaps heard, but the
pass_b_english: —to finish the telling, she brings the shameless counsel. She does not even say openly, "Blaspheme." Evil advisers dare not introduce counsel uncovered. What are you saying, woman? One ought to propitiate and reconcile — and you advise provocation? If God did these things, entreat him; do not blaspheme. And how is it clear that I die as a beloved one? See how she held blasphemy: as if she thought it could bring death on her at once.

"[[If we received good things from the Lord’s hand, shall we not also bear the bad? >> Bible:Job 2:10]]" Struck from every side, the blessed man stood more securely. Countless arrows did not make him yield; he emptied the devil’s quiver and did not fall. Like an excellent pilot he was not sunk when the sea raged, and not careless when it was calm; in both seasons he kept the same skill. Wealth did not puff him up, poverty did not crush him; fair weather did not leave him slack, and nearly total ruin did not shake his courage. Let rich and poor hear: the story helps both prosperity and calamity. Handling both weapons, the contestant of piety — crown-bearer of the inhabited world — raised a trophy in each and met every kind of demonic war.

As a soldier trained for night fighting, walls, land, sea, bow, spear, sling, and javelin conquers everywhere, so this noble man bore every trial with courage: poverty, hunger, disease, pain, loss of children, friends, enemies, wife, and servants. No human calamity failed to empty itself into that body; still he rose above every net and higher than the devil’s reeds. More marvelous still: everything came at once, in excess, under one blow — not little by little. Other people rarely meet all together. Poverty may leave health; poverty and disease may still leave a consoling wife as a harbor; if not such a wife, still not one advising ruin; if children die, not all at once; if at once, not by such a death; if by such a death, still comforting friends; if not comforters, still not insulting; if insulting, still not servants reproaching and spitting in the face; if that, still not such disease on a dunghill without shelter or a hand stretched out. Job endured all of it.

"[[Each came from his own country: Eliphaz king of the Temanites, Baldad tyrant of the Saucheans, Sophar king of the Minaeans >> Bible:Job 2:11]]." Friendly presence; friendly exhortation. Name-glosses: Eliphaz — "God scattered me," or "contempt of my God"; Teman — their eclipse; Sophar — watcher or contempt; Baldad — aging and glorious; Saucheans — idle talk.
